column3: Description
Standard two‑field form (email/username + password) with a “Remember me” checkbox and submit button.
Collects name, email, password, and confirm‑password, plus an optional terms‑of‑service checkbox.
Colored bar beneath the password field that updates from “Weak” to “Strong” in real‑time.
Eye icon inside password input that switches masking on and off.
Single email field plus “Send reset link” button.
New‑password + confirm‑password fields shown after following a reset link.
Email field that sends a one‑click sign‑in link instead of asking for a password.
Six one‑digit boxes for typing an SMS or authenticator‑app code.
Shows a list of one‑time backup codes with a “Download as TXT” button.
Modal prompting to approve or deny a new device sign‑in, often with location info.
Dropdown to pick a question plus answer field—used as fallback verification.
Large “Sign in with SSO” button that triggers a corporate identity provider flow.
Row of branded buttons (Google, Apple, GitHub) for quick third‑party sign‑in.
Embedded reCAPTCHA widget verifying the user is not a bot.
Background captcha that validates quietly without extra user action.
Full page explaining the account is locked after too many failed attempts and offering support contact.
Dismissible bar reminding users to confirm their email with a “Resend link” action.
Simple email input + resend button, used when the original verification link expired.
Pops up after inactivity, displaying countdown and “Stay signed in” button.
Avatar button listing multiple user accounts to switch between quickly.
Circular image placeholder with “Upload / Replace” action during sign‑up.
Inline message showing green check or red error as the user types a desired username.
Scrollable legal text shown during registration with “I Agree” button.
Separate checkboxes for marketing, analytics, and personalization consent.
WebAuthn‑powered action that uses device biometrics (Face ID, Touch ID) instead of a password.
Displays a QR code users scan in Google Authenticator or Authy to enable 2‑factor codes.
Mobile‑optimized field that auto‑reads incoming SMS verification codes.
Confirmation screen instructing users to check their inbox for a magic‑login link.
Confirms new email and asks for current password before updating.
Blocking modal explaining consequences with “Deactivate / Cancel” buttons.
Requires users to type “DELETE” or their email to confirm irreversible deletion.
Brief toast message welcoming the user by name after successful login.
Small modal requesting current password before sensitive settings can be changed.
Tab inside profile showing 2‑FA status, recent logins, and device list.
Table of devices, IPs, and timestamps with “Log out remote session” option.
Template email with “Was this you? Yes / No” links for unfamiliar logins.
Prompts user to enter a 6‑digit code sent to their email instead of a password.
Native browser prompt requesting fingerprint or face scan for authentication.
Invisible background check; only displays a banner when extra verification is needed.
Dialog explaining how to save recovery codes as a CSV file for safekeeping.
User types corporate email; the page auto‑routes to the correct SAML/OIDC identity provider.
Branded buttons for Okta, Azure AD, Google Workspace, etc., letting federated users choose their IdP.
Minimal page with company logo and spinner shown while the browser redirects between SP and IdP.
Full‑page message stating “You’ve been signed out by your organization” with a “Sign In Again” button.
Blocking dialog that requires users to set up MFA before they can proceed inside the app.
Input field tailored for 6‑ or 8‑digit codes generated by YubiKey or RSA tokens.
Browser‑level dialog requesting a client certificate—common in government or finance sectors.
Modal triggered mid‑session asking for password re‑entry or OTP before accessing high‑risk resources.
Yellow strip appearing X days before password expiry with “Change Password” CTA.
Screen that forces password change upon next login due to policy expiration.
Admin view listing synced users/groups with last‑sync timestamps and error badges.
Avatar menu item allowing privileged users to assume another role (e.g., “View as Reader”).
Popup listing requested scopes (“Read email”, “Manage calendars”) with “Allow / Deny”.
Warns of unusual login location and asks for extra verification code.
Admin overlay offering CSV export of authentication events with date‑range picker.
